tep_native_channel.interpretation: if a fraction f of astrated mass transits a spallation-active surface and returns with D mass fraction eps_D, closure requires f x eps_D = 2.04e-05.  E.g. eps_D = 1e-2 (strong spallation zone) needs f = 2.0e-3; eps_D = 1e-4 needs f = 0.20; enrichment only to the ISM level (eps_D = X_D_ISM) requires f = 0.6 — every astrated parcel must pass through the zone, which no surface geometry supplies.  In eternal cosmology the emissivity rate is NOT the bottleneck (external exposure is unbounded); the bottleneck is the fraction of baryons cycled through the producing geometry per astration epoch.

verdict: The standing ISM D/H requires a yield of 2.0e-5 D per unit astrated mass.  Documented channels supply 10^-7-10^-8 — shortfalls of 120-2000x.  A TEP-native well-adjacent spallation channel closes the ledger only if the processed fraction f satisfies f x eps_D = 2.0e-5; the viability condition is a throughput statement, computable once the horizon-transport solution fixes eps_D.  Gate D item d1 remains open but is now a quantified budget rather than an open-ended debt.
